title: Relational model: tables, keys, constraints, when to bend the rules
summary: Why Codd's 1970 relational model still wins on data integrity, what each normal form actually buys, where surrogate vs natural keys diverge, when JSONB and arrays beat a side table, and why some hyperscale shops disable foreign keys.
crux: Tables, keys, constraints, normalization — fifty-five years old, still load-bearing. Bend deliberately, not accidentally.
keytakeaway: The relational model is fifty-five years old and still load-bearing: tables, keys, FKs, constraints, normalization (target 3NF, bend deliberately). Postgres types matter; JSONB is the long-tail escape hatch, not the primary storage.

title: Indexes in PostgreSQL: B-tree, GIN, GiST, BRIN, and the cost of a wrong one
summary: How Postgres indexes are built (B-tree, GIN, GiST, BRIN, SP-GiST, hash), why the leading-column rule is the most violated principle in production, how partial / expression / covering indexes change the cost model, and when to add or drop one.
crux: Indexes = sorted copies of data for one question. Leading-column rule. Every index taxes every write. Pick deliberately.
keytakeaway: Indexes are sorted copies of data for one query. B-tree is default; GIN/GiST/BRIN for non-ordered types. Leading-column rule is iron. CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, INCLUDE for covering, partial for hot subsets. Audit quarterly.

title: Execution plans in PostgreSQL: reading EXPLAIN, fixing row-estimate disasters
summary: How the Postgres planner builds an execution plan from statistics, how to read EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN ANALYZE, why bad row estimates produce 1000× slowdowns, and the operational discipline of statistics maintenance, extended statistics, and plan-cache control.
crux: EXPLAIN shows the plan. The plan is a guess from statistics. Rows estimated vs actual is the most diagnostic number in the database.
keytakeaway: Plans are the planner's guess. Statistics drive the guess. ANALYZE, default_statistics_target, CREATE STATISTICS for correlated columns. Read EXPLAIN ANALYZE: rows-estimated vs rows-actual is the diagnostic. Tune random_page_cost for SSD. plan_cache_mode = force_custom_plan for skewed prepared statements. auto_explain + pg_stat_statements is the observability backbone.

title: MVCC and isolation in PostgreSQL: snapshots, anomalies, bloat
summary: How Postgres lets thousands of readers and writers share rows without blocking, what isolation actually guarantees, and why one long transaction can swell a table by 100 GB.
crux: How Postgres lets many writers and readers see consistent data at once — and what it costs to keep that promise.
keytakeaway: MVCC trades a fixed storage tax (every UPDATE writes a new tuple, every snapshot pins old ones) for unblocked reads + writes. Isolation level decides which anomalies you tolerate; bloat discipline keeps the tax bounded.

title: Connection pooling in PostgreSQL: PgBouncer modes, sizing math, and pool-exhaustion failure modes
summary: Why Postgres backends are heavyweight, how PgBouncer's session/transaction/statement modes change app contracts, the math behind pool sizing, the prepared-statement transaction-mode trap (and PgBouncer 1.21+ fix), and the Supavisor/Odyssey/PgCat landscape.
crux: Postgres backends are heavy. Pool to multiplex. Transaction mode breaks SET / session prepares / advisory locks unless you adapt.
keytakeaway: Postgres backends are heavy. Pool to multiplex: client-pool inside each worker, PgBouncer (transaction mode, 1.21+, prepared statements on) in front of Postgres. Size pool as (cores × 2) + spindles; do not raise to fix exhaustion — find the hold. idle_in_transaction_session_timeout = 60s is free insurance. Observability: cl_waiting, idle-in-tx age, pool-checkout latency.

title: Schema migrations in PostgreSQL: locks, expand-contract, and the lock-queue failure mode
summary: Why ALTER TABLE behind a long-running query freezes the database, the Postgres lock matrix, expand-contract for breaking changes, ADD COLUMN / NOT NULL / type-change safety, CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY discipline, pgroll and Atlas in 2026.
crux: ALTER TABLE takes AccessExclusiveLock. Lock queue is FIFO. SET lock_timeout. Expand-contract for breaking changes.
keytakeaway: ALTER TABLE takes AccessExclusiveLock; lock queue is FIFO; SET lock_timeout = '2s' is mandatory. ADD COLUMN with constant default is instant since PG 11. NOT VALID + VALIDATE for constraints. CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY for indexes. Breaking changes (rename, drop, type-change) decompose into expand-contract over days. Squawk lints in CI; pgroll/Atlas automate; Prisma/Drizzle run.

title: Sharding PostgreSQL: shard keys, hot-shard failure mode, partitioning vs Citus
summary: When one Postgres is not enough — shard-key selection, hash/range/list/directory strategies, declarative partitioning vs Citus, co-location, the hot-shard failure mode, online resharding, schema-based sharding.
crux: Sharding splits one DB by shard key. Co-location is the win; hot shards are the failure mode; resharding online is the test.
keytakeaway: Sharding splits Postgres across many instances by a shard key (tenant_id for B2B SaaS). Co-location of tenant-scoped tables on the same key is the central invariant — keeps 99% of queries single-shard. Failure mode is hot shard from skewed tenant; isolate large tenants via Citus's primitive. Cross-shard queries: push analytics to OLAP via CDC. Reshard online with logical replication. Don't pre-shard.
